speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of chronic swelling, family involvement, and a prior DVT is concerning for venous stasis; can you describe the wound's edges and the color of the overlying skin? REQUEST TEST: Venous_Doppler_Ultrasound to check for chronic venous insufficiency or residual obstruction.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Stasis Ulcer. The presence of a 6-month non-healing wound on the right lower leg, combined with a 10-year history of edema, family history, prior DVT, and Doppler confirmation of venous reflux/obstruction, confirms this diagnosis.
